statement: For fixed gamma in (0,2), the scalar identities Q=2/gamma+gamma/2 and xi=gamma/d do not uniquely specify a positive value d. At gamma=1, both (d,xi,Q)=(3,1/3,5/2) and (4,1/4,5/2) satisfy them.
assumptions: Only the two displayed scalar identities and positivity of d and xi are supplied; no metric construction or LFPP exponent equation is supplied.

source.attribution: Independent algebraic non-identifiability deduction; not a metric construction

proof_or_counterexample: Substitute the two triples into the identities. More generally any d>0 determines xi=gamma/d without changing Q.
remaining_gap: Independent review pending; an evaluated relation Q(xi) or an equivalent actual LFPP estimate remains missing. The two scalar triples are not claimed to satisfy the full metric axioms.

type: counterexample to dropping a source hypothesis
statement: For every fixed gamma in (0,2), let h be a whole-plane GFF, U a nonempty deterministic open planar domain, D_h its gamma-LQG metric, Q=2/gamma+gamma/2 and xi=gamma/d_gamma. The field-dependent gamma-thick set X=T_h^gamma intersect U has Euclidean Hausdorff dimension 2-gamma^2/2 and D_h Hausdorff dimension d_gamma almost surely. Substituting X into the independent-set metric KPZ identity falsely predicts Euclidean dimension 2, with residual gamma^2/2>0.
assumptions: Canonical subcritical gamma-LQG metric
Gamma fixed in (0,2)
Circle-average thick points as defined by Gwynne-Pfeffer equation (1.10)
The independent-set premise is deliberately absent for X=T_h^gamma

source.quote: a random Borel set independent from h

proof_or_counterexample: Source equations give the two dimensions. Compute xi Q d_gamma-xi^2 d_gamma^2/2=gamma Q-gamma^2/2=2. The actual Euclidean dimension is 2-gamma^2/2.
remaining_gap: No gap in the displayed implication from the cited theorems; independent referee check pending. This does not compute d_gamma.

statement: At gamma=sqrt(8/3), the metric KPZ equality for independent sets cannot apply to the image of a nonconstant D_h-geodesic. The geodesic has D_h Hausdorff dimension 1; since d_gamma=4, xi=1/sqrt(6), Q=5/sqrt(6), the equality would give Euclidean Hausdorff dimension 5/6-1/12=3/4. A nonconstant Euclidean-continuous path has Euclidean Hausdorff dimension at least 1.
assumptions: Canonical sqrt(8/3)-LQG metric inducing the Euclidean topology
A nonconstant finite-distance D_h-geodesic parametrized by D_h length
Known exact value d_sqrt(8/3)=4
proof_or_counterexample: The geodesic is isometric to a nondegenerate interval in its induced metric. Its Euclidean image is connected and contains distinct endpoints a,b. The Euclidean 1-Lipschitz map z -> |z-a| sends that image onto a set containing [0,|b-a|], so its Euclidean Hausdorff dimension is at least one. This contradicts 3/4.
remaining_gap: Independent referee check pending. The contradiction rejects an invalid theorem application, not the LQG metric or the source theorem.

statement: For finite nonempty paths with positive deterministic vertex weights, centered Gaussian X with any PSD covariance C, and beta>0, m_beta(xi)=E[-beta^-1 log sum_p exp(-beta log sum_v a_pv exp(xi X_v))] obeys m_beta'(xi)=xi E[A_beta-beta B_beta], with A_beta and B_beta as defined in FINITE_BRIDGE_INDEPENDENT.md, both nonnegative. The integrated derivative tends to E log D_b-E log D_a as beta tends to infinity for each fixed finite path family and 0<=a<b<infinity.
assumptions: Finite nonempty family of nonempty paths
Positive deterministic path weights
Centered finite Gaussian vector
Covariance positive semidefinite, possibly singular
Fixed finite family when beta tends to infinity
source: w525/STATEMENT_FOR_ADVERSARY.md (statement only); independent proof in FINITE_BRIDGE_INDEPENDENT.md
proof_or_counterexample: Differentiate the log-sum-exp twice; apply Gaussian integration by parts with X=C^(1/2)Z; A is a weighted sum of Var(X_i-X_j)/2 and B is a weighted C-variance of gradients; use uniform soft-min error log|P|/beta only after integrating.
remaining_gap: No numerical LFPP exponent computed. Uniformity in growing path family and referee check remain.

statement: Beta_n tending to infinity does not suffice for soft-min/hard-min agreement after division by L_n on growing finite Gaussian path families. Take L_n=n, N_n=2^(n^2) singleton paths with unit weights and X_i=Z for a common standard normal Z. Then log D_xi=xi Z while F_beta_n(xi X)=xi Z-n log 2 for beta_n=n. Their normalized expectations differ by -log 2 for every n. A sufficient uniform-error premise is log|P_n|/(beta_n L_n) -> 0.
assumptions: General finite Gaussian path model with PSD covariance; no claim to realize a planar LFPP network
Fixed xi>=0
n is a positive integer
All-ones covariance and unit weights
proof_or_counterexample: All path energies coincide, so the exponential sum gains exactly N_n identical terms. The hard minimum is xi Z and the smoothing penalty is log N_n/beta_n=n log 2. Divide by n. The sufficient premise follows from 0<=min f_p-F_beta<=log|P|/beta.
remaining_gap: Need a uniform effective-entropy estimate and an actual two-dimensional LFPP evaluation of the interpolation term, not merely this finite counterexample.

type: integrated-response counterexample without uniform smoothing control
statement: For L_n=beta_n=n and M_n=2^(n^2), take M_n deterministic-zero-field singleton paths of weight exp(n), plus one path of M_n independent N(0,n) fields each of weight 1/M_n. The covariance satisfies v_n=n=O(L_n). Hard-min median log exponents at xi=0 and xi=2 are respectively 0 and 1 after division by L_n, for all sufficiently large n. The normalized hard-min expected endpoint difference tends to 1, while the beta_n-soft-min expected endpoint difference and its exact integrated Gaussian response tend to 1-log 2. Thus beta_n->infinity, covariance growth, and convergent hard-min endpoint medians do not alone suffice for the integrated reduction.
assumptions: General finite Gaussian path model; not asserted to be a planar LFPP discretization
Positive deterministic weights
PSD diagonal covariance, allowing deterministic zero coordinates
Fixed endpoints 0 and 2
No uniform entropy-error premise is imposed
source: Independent campaign derivation in FINITE_BRIDGE_INDEPENDENT.md, C526.6 paragraph
proof_or_counterexample: For S_n=(1/M_n) sum exp(2 sqrt(n) Z_i), E S_n=exp(2n) and relative variance=(exp(4n)-1)/M_n. Chebyshev gives P(S_n<exp(n))->0. Jensen gives log S_n>=2 sqrt(n) Z_bar with E|2 sqrt(n) Z_bar|=2 sqrt(2n/(pi M_n)). Therefore E min(c n,log S_n)/n->c for c=1 and c=1-log2. The hard value uses c=1, the soft value uses c=1-log2 with error at most log2/n. At xi=0 both normalized values tend to zero. Full proof saved independently; no large family computed.
remaining_gap: Independent referee check pending. The proof as read from w525 already includes a sufficient uniform entropy bound and is not refuted by this example. Exact planar-LFPP response remains unevaluated.
